editorial:
Imagine you are a young, hopeful writer who finally gets a chance to put your play on Broadway, but there is a huge catch. Your bankroll is a scary mob boss named Nick Valenti. To make things worse, Nick insists that his girlfriend, Olive, get the lead role. The problem is that Olive is completely clueless and can't act her way out of a paper bag. You get to watch this poor writer struggle through rehearsals with a cast of weirdos, including a lead actor who cannot stop eating and a diva who wants to change every line. It is a funny, chaotic ride that feels like a backstage nightmare where one wrong move could get you whacked.

You will love how the tension builds as the opening night gets closer. The acting is top-notch, and the dialogue is snappy and fast. While some parts feel a bit like an old-school play, the humor keeps it moving. If you enjoy comedies about art and crime, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you really love the style, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head on opening night when the play is a total disaster because Olive is so bad. The mob boss, Nick, realizes his girlfriend is a joke and is embarrassed in front of everyone. He ends up killing Olive in a fit of rage. However, the writer survives the chaos. In the end, the play actually becomes a hit because the real-life drama and the scandal surrounding the deaths make everyone want to see it.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves comedies with a crime twist.
